name: Manali
short_description: Alpine valleys, river gorges, and gateway to high Himalayan passes.
description: Manali sits in the Kullu Valley along the Beas River, surrounded by deodar forests and snow-capped peaks. It blends adventure sports, café culture, and access to Rohtang and Atal Tunnel routes toward Lahaul-Spiti.
overview: A classic hill station base for trekking, paragliding, and road trips toward higher valleys. Acclimatize before pushing to very high passes.
weather_summary: Pleasant summers; cold winters with snow at higher trails. Monsoon brings landslide risk on mountain roads.
best_time: March–June and September–November for clear skies; December–February for snow experiences.

name: Leh-Ladakh
short_description: High-altitude desert, ancient monasteries, and dramatic mountain passes.
description: Leh is the heart of Ladakh—arid peaks, Buddhist heritage, and routes to Nubra, Pangong, and remote villages. Altitude and thin air demand gradual acclimatization.
overview: Plan rest days in Leh, carry sun protection and layers, and respect inner-line permit rules for protected areas.
weather_summary: Cold desert climate—intense sun, cool nights, and winter road closures on high passes.
best_time: May–September when most passes are open; avoid rushed itineraries at altitude.
gear: Buff / scarf for dust and cold

name: Kedarnath
short_description: Sacred Shiva shrine set among towering Garhwal peaks.
description: The trek to Kedarnath follows the Mandakini valley through steep stone paths to one of the holiest Char Dham sites. Weather can change rapidly at altitude.
overview: A demanding pilgrimage trek—register in advance, check helicopter and pony options if needed, and carry warm layers year-round.
weather_summary: Cool to cold; afternoon clouds common during monsoon window. Winter closure of the shrine route.
best_time: May–June and September–October (pre/post monsoon) for safer trekking windows.

name: Badrinath
short_description: Pilgrimage town beneath Nilkantha peak along the Alaknanda.
description: Badrinath hosts the iconic Vishnu temple at roughly 3,300 m. The journey combines road access with short walks; altitude and cold evenings matter even when the walk feels easier than Kedarnath.
overview: Road-linked pilgrimage hub—still plan for registration, weather delays, and layered clothing for temple visits and short hikes.
weather_summary: Cold nights year-round; monsoon can affect road connectivity on the route from Rishikesh.
best_time: May–June and September–October for stable mountain weather.

name: Auli
short_description: Meadows and ski slopes with Nanda Devi views.
description: Auli is a high meadow known for winter skiing and cable-car views across the Garhwal Himalaya. Gentle walks suit relaxation while nearby trails add adventure.
overview: Ideal for scenic chairlift rides, photography, and short alpine walks. Ski season needs advance gear or rentals.
weather_summary: Crisp and sunny in peak season; heavy snow in deep winter affecting road access.
best_time: December–March for snow sports; April–June for meadows and clearer trekking weather.

name: Mussoorie
short_description: Queen of the Hills—Mall Road, Doon views, colonial charm.
description: Mussoorie overlooks the Doon Valley from the Garhwal foothills. Gun Hill, Kempty Falls, and Camel Back Road are classics; winter line views draw photographers.
weather_summary: Cool summers; cold winters. Monsoon fog and slippery trails on outlying walks.
best_time: March–June and September–November; December–January for crisp mountain air.
overview: Queen of the Hills—Mall Road, Doon views, colonial charm.

name: Nainital
short_description: Lake district of Kumaon—Naini Lake, boats, and forested ridges.
description: Nainital wraps around Naini Lake at roughly 2,000 m. Boating, Snow View, and Naina Devi Temple anchor visits; nearby Sattal and Bhimtal extend trips.
weather_summary: Mild summers; chilly winters with occasional snow on ridges. Monsoon lake mists.
overview: Lake district of Kumaon—Naini Lake, boats, and forested ridges.

name: Rishikesh
short_description: Ganga ghats, yoga capital, and white-water gateway to Garhwal.
description: Rishikesh sits where the Ganga leaves the Shivaliks. Ashrams, Laxman Jhula, and Class II–IV rapids make it a hub for wellness and adventure before higher hills.
weather_summary: Warm pre-monsoon; heavy monsoon rains. Pleasant October–March.
best_time: Late September–May for rafting; avoid peak monsoon.
overview: Ganga ghats, yoga capital, and white-water gateway to Garhwal.

name: Ranikhet
short_description: Quiet cantonment meadows and Himalayan views in Almora district.
description: Ranikhet offers golf, pine forests, and views of Nanda Devi range. It is calmer than crowded hill stations and suits slow travel.
weather_summary: Pleasant summers; cold winters. Clear skies in post-monsoon.
overview: Quiet cantonment meadows and Himalayan views in Almora district.

name: Kausani
short_description: Panoramas of Trishul and Nanda Devi—tea gardens and quiet ridges.
description: Kausani is often called the Switzerland of India for its 300 km Himalayan views. Tea estates and Anasakti Ashram add culture to the vistas.
weather_summary: Cool year-round; winter snow possible. Monsoon clouds obscure peaks.
overview: Panoramas of Trishul and Nanda Devi—tea gardens and quiet ridges.

name: Almora
short_description: Kumaoni culture, cobbled bazaars, and temple architecture.
description: Almora is a tiered ridge town with Kasar Devi, Bright End Corner, and access to Binsar and Jageshwar. Rich in handicrafts and local cuisine.
weather_summary: Temperate; monsoon heavy. Winters cool.
overview: Kumaoni culture, cobbled bazaars, and temple architecture.

name: Lansdowne
short_description: Garhwal Rifles town—deodar forests and unhurried walks.
description: Lansdowne is a cantonment hill station with Bhulla Lake, Tip-n-Top views, and minimal commercialization compared to bigger resorts.
weather_summary: Pleasant summers; cold winters with occasional snow.
overview: Garhwal Rifles town—deodar forests and unhurried walks.

name: Chopta
short_description: Mini Switzerland—base for Tungnath and Chandrashila treks.
description: Chopta sits near 2,700 m in Rudraprayag district. Rhododendron forests and the trek to the highest Shiva temple at Tungnath define the experience.
weather_summary: Cold nights even in summer; heavy winter snow. Monsoon trails slippery.
best_time: April–June and September–November; winter for snow trekkers with gear.
overview: Mini Switzerland—base for Tungnath and Chandrashila treks.

name: Dhanaulti
short_description: Deodar eco-parks and snow glimpses without Mussoorie crowds.
description: Dhanaulti is a quieter alternative above the Doon, known for Surkanda Devi trek access and eco-park walks among oak and deodar.
weather_summary: Cool; winter snow possible. Monsoon lush but misty.
best_time: March–June and October–February for snow seekers.
overview: Deodar eco-parks and snow glimpses without Mussoorie crowds.

name: Pithoragarh
short_description: Little Kashmir—gateway to Johar, Milam, and Nepal border routes.
description: Pithoragarh is the eastern Kumaon hub with deep valleys and views of Panchachuli. It suits trek planners heading toward remote border areas.
weather_summary: Monsoon heavy; winters cold. Pre-monsoon thunderstorms.
overview: Little Kashmir—gateway to Johar, Milam, and Nepal border routes.

name: Kanatal
short_description: Secluded ridge campfires and Tehri views above Chamba road.
description: Kanatal is a small hamlet known for camping, Surkanda approaches, and apple orchards—popular with Delhi weekenders seeking quiet.
weather_summary: Cool; winter snow. Monsoon road checks needed.
overview: Secluded ridge campfires and Tehri views above Chamba road.

name: Chakrata
short_description: Dehradun district cantonment—Tiger Falls and deodar solitude.
description: Chakrata offers waterfall hikes, Budher caves, and strict forest schedules. Foreign nationals may need permits—check current rules before travel.
weather_summary: Pleasant summers; cold winters. Monsoon landslide risk on approach roads.
overview: Dehradun district cantonment—Tiger Falls and deodar solitude.

name: Munsiyari
short_description: Panchachuli base—high trails and Johar valley culture.
description: Munsiyari sits at the Gori Ganga valley head with dramatic Panchachuli views. It is the start for Milam, Ralam, and Khalia Top treks.
weather_summary: Cold winters with snow; monsoon road disruptions.
overview: Panchachuli base—high trails and Johar valley culture.

name: Harsil
short_description: Bhagirathi hamlet—apple orchards on the road to Gangotri.
description: Harsil is a scenic village before Gangotri with alpine walks and the Dharali–Gangotri corridor. Ideal for acclimatization and photography.
weather_summary: Cold; winter road closures toward Gangotri. Monsoon cautious driving.
overview: Bhagirathi hamlet—apple orchards on the road to Gangotri.

name: Gangotri
short_description: Ganga origin shrine—gateway to Gaumukh trek.
description: Gangotri temple marks the spiritual source of the Bhagirathi. Trekkers continue toward Gaumukh and Tapovan with permits and guides.
weather_summary: Cold; heavy winter snow. Short summer window for full access.
overview: Ganga origin shrine—gateway to Gaumukh trek.

name: Yamunotri
short_description: Yamuna glacier shrine—Char Dham trek from Janki Chatti.
description: Yamunotri is the western Char Dham site. The trek from Janki Chatti crosses rugged terrain to the hot-spring precinct at the temple.
weather_summary: Cold; monsoon landslides on approach roads.
overview: Yamuna glacier shrine—Char Dham trek from Janki Chatti.

name: Joshimath
short_description: Winter seat of Badrinath—cable car hub to Auli and valley access.
description: Joshimath is a strategic Garhwal town for pilgrims and skiers. It links to Auli ropeway, Valley of Flowers (seasonal), and Hemkund routes.
weather_summary: Cold winters; monsoon travel delays common on mountain roads.
overview: Winter seat of Badrinath—cable car hub to Auli and valley access.

name: Uttarkashi
short_description: Gateway town on the route to Gangotri and Dodital treks.
description: Uttarkashi on the Bhagirathi offers temples, trekking outfitters, and logistics before higher Garhwal valleys.
weather_summary: Warm summers relative to high hills; monsoon river rise.
overview: Gateway town on the route to Gangotri and Dodital treks.

name: Haridwar
short_description: Ganga aarti at Har Ki Pauri—pilgrim gateway to the Char Dham.
description: Haridwar is one of Hinduism’s seven holy cities. Evening aarti, ghats, and access to Rishikesh and the mountain yatra routes define visits.
weather_summary: Hot summers; pleasant winters. Monsoon humid.
overview: Ganga aarti at Har Ki Pauri—pilgrim gateway to the Char Dham.

name: Mukteshwar
short_description: Fruit belt views—Nanda Devi and peaceful Kumaon orchards.
description: Mukteshwar offers cliff viewpoints, IVRI campus walks, and a quiet alternative to crowded Nainital.
weather_summary: Cool; winter frost. Monsoon lush.
overview: Fruit belt views—Nanda Devi and peaceful Kumaon orchards.
